sam (eng-sre): Heads-up — we're sketching a capacity-aware rate limiter to protect the GPU fleet during spikes. Thinking token-bucket per API key with an org-level bucket that drains faster when the fleet is saturated. Thoughts?

irene (eng-platform): +1 on hierarchical buckets. Per-key for fairness, org-level to enforce org-level commit. Important: refill rates should be adaptive to available GPU slots, not static.

alex (infra): Agree. Practical formula we used before: refill_rate = base_rate * max(min_factor, available_slots / total_slots). Keeps some baseline throughput even at full saturation. Example: min_factor=0.1.

maria (runtime): Also add short-lived admission queues per-region/model. If a request can't get tokens, either 429 with Retry-After or enqueue to a small bounded FIFO (5-10s). Prefer enqueue only for same-org internal retries. For public API, 429 is simpler.

sam (eng-sre): Nice. How do we compute available_slots reliably at edge? Local caches will diverge.

irene (eng-platform): Use a hybrid: central capacity estimator publishes periodic snapshots (1s-5s), edge keeps local token bucket and a multiplier from last snapshot. Edge admission uses local bucket * multiplier. On disconnect, fall back to conservative multiplier.

alex (infra): Pseudocode we tested:```
# refill tokens per second
refill = base_rate * max(0.1, available_slots / total_slots)
bucket_tokens = min(capacity, bucket_tokens + refill * elapsed)
```
Keep math in doubles, but enforce integer token consumption per request.

maria (runtime): Need fairness: weighted token-buckets (weight = plan tier) + weighted fair queueing for queued requests to avoid noisy neighbors. Also track metrics: token_requests, tokens_granted, tokens_denied, queue_length, 429_rate per org/key/model-region.

sam (eng-sre): For burst handling, allow short bursts if org has unused burst budget. But cap burst window and tie budget refill to long-term commit. Otherwise big customers can starve small ones during backfill.

irene (eng-platform): Also consider circuit-breaker style: if queue latency or GPU tail latency crosses thresholds, switch to aggressive shedding (reduce multiplier, raise min_factor) and emit alert.

ratebot: rule-update: capacity-aware-rate-limiter ON for canary (10% of edge nodes).

sam (eng-sre): Excellent. Action items: 1) prototype edge-local token-bucket with periodic multiplier (alex + irene), 2) define metrics plan (maria), 3) policy doc for per-key/org hierarchy + burst rules (sam). We'll keep enqueue behavior conservative.

irene (eng-platform): I'll draft a short doc with diagrams and the formulas. Putting it in /docs once ready.

sam (eng-sre): Thanks — will follow up with a short design PR next week. :thumbsup:
